series.title: Seoul Starter · 서울 생활
series.description: Jisoo has just moved to Seoul for a new job. Follow her first days in the city: a friendly neighbor, convenience stores, subway lines and a brand-new office.
series.style_prompt: Bright, clean Korean webtoon style with crisp line art and soft cel shading; modern Seoul streets, small red-brick apartment buildings, convenience stores, offices and subway stations; soft natural daylight, warm pastel palette, friendly expressive faces. No text, letters or speech bubbles in the image.

characters.name: Jisoo
characters.appearance_prompt: Korean woman, 28, shoulder-length straight black hair with soft see-through bangs, warm brown eyes, slim build; casual look: cream knit cardigan over a white T-shirt, light-blue jeans, white sneakers and a small tan crossbody bag; office look: navy blazer over a white blouse. Bright, slightly nervous smile.

characters.name: Minho
characters.appearance_prompt: Korean man, 28, tall, short tousled dark-brown hair, friendly crescent-shaped eyes and an easy grin; at home a gray hoodie, black joggers and slippers, outside a navy bomber jacket with earphones around his neck. Relaxed, helpful body language.

characters.name: Yuna
characters.appearance_prompt: Korean woman, 31, chin-length dark bob tucked behind one ear, small silver earrings, the same friendly crescent-shaped eyes as her younger brother Minho; office look: beige blouse, navy slacks, ID badge on a lanyard. Confident, warm, big-sister energy.

characters.name: Clerk
characters.appearance_prompt: Young Korean man, early 20s, convenience-store clerk, short neat black hair, round glasses, green-and-white store uniform vest over a white shirt with a plain blank name tag (no writing), polite cheerful expression.

characters.name: Team Leader Kim
characters.appearance_prompt: Korean man in his late 40s, neatly combed short black hair with a little gray at the temples, rectangular glasses, dark suit, white shirt and navy tie; calm, kind but serious expression.

episode.title: 이사하는 날 · Moving Day
episode.synopsis: Jisoo arrives in Seoul with too many heavy boxes and moves into a small apartment building. Her friendly next-door neighbor Minho introduces himself and insists on helping even when she politely refuses. By evening she is exhausted but happy: a new home, a new neighbor and a new life in Seoul.

panels.image_prompt: Wide establishing shot of a quiet residential street in Seoul on a sunny spring morning: a four-story red-brick apartment building with small balconies, a small moving truck at the curb, Jisoo standing in front with a big suitcase and a stack of cardboard boxes, looking up at the building with excited, sparkling eyes. Cherry blossom petals in the air, soft daylight, no text.

bubbles.translation: Today Jisoo is moving to Seoul.

tokens.note: 은/는 marks the topic, what the sentence is about.
(으)로 marks direction: 서울로 = to Seoul.
Target word: 이사하다 means moving to a new home, not 'move' in general.
The plain -다 form is used for exclamations and thoughts to yourself.

panels.image_prompt: Jisoo struggling to carry a big cardboard box up a narrow concrete staircase inside the building, cheeks puffed, a sweat drop on her forehead, more boxes piled at the bottom of the stairs. Warm light through a small stairwell window.

bubbles.translation: Ugh, all this stuff is so heavy...

tokens.lemma_translation: oh my (sigh of effort, pain or surprise)
tokens.note: 아이고 is the classic Korean sigh for effort, tiredness or surprise.
Target word: 짐 = bags, boxes, things you carry or move. 이/가 marks the subject.
Target word: 무겁다 is ㅂ-irregular: 무겁 + 어 → 무거워. Casual because she's talking to herself.

panels.image_prompt: The apartment door next to Jisoo's on the same floor opens; Minho, a friendly young man in a gray hoodie and slippers, leans out with a curious, welcoming smile, looking toward Jisoo and her boxes in the hallway.

bubbles.translation: Hi there! Did you just move in?

tokens.lemma_translation: to be well, at peace (used in greetings)
tokens.note: Target word: the everyday polite 'hello' (literally 'are you at peace?'), fine at any time of day.
이사 오다 = to move in (here); 이사 가다 = to move away (there).
-시- adds respect for the person you're talking about, polite with a new neighbor.

panels.image_prompt: Jisoo, still hugging the box, turns toward Minho with a surprised but bright smile and gives a small polite nod of the head.

tokens.lemma_translation: to be well, at peace (used in greetings)

tokens.note: 저 is the humble 'I' for people you speak politely to; the casual 'I' is 나.

breakdown.meaning: am, is (polite copula after a vowel)

tokens.note: Name + 예요 (after a vowel) / 이에요 (after a consonant) = 'I am …'.

panels.image_prompt: Minho steps into the hallway, rubbing the back of his head with a shy grin; Jisoo smiles back. A bright corridor with two apartment doors side by side.

bubbles.translation: Nice to meet you! I'm Minho. I live next door.

tokens.note: Target word: 반가워요 = 'Nice to meet you', friendly and polite. ㅂ-irregular like 무겁다.
에 marks where something is or where you live: 옆집에 살아요 = I live next door.

bubbles.translation: Oh, so we're neighbors! Nice to meet you.

tokens.note: Target word: 이웃 = neighbor. -네요 shows you've just realized something.

panels.image_prompt: Minho looks at the pile of cardboard boxes by the stairs and rolls up his sleeves with a helpful expression; Jisoo waves both hands in front of her chest, politely refusing, a little embarrassed.

bubbles.translation: That's a lot of stuff. I'll help you.

tokens.note: 저 + 가 becomes 제가: 'I' as the subject.
Target word: 도와주다 = to help. -ㄹ게요 = 'I'll do it (for you)', an offer or promise.
아니에요 is a polite 'Oh no, it's fine' when you turn down an offer.
Target word: 괜찮아요 = 'It's fine'. It also works as a polite 'No, thank you'.

panels.image_prompt: Minho has already lifted the biggest box with a confident grin and heads toward Jisoo's door; Jisoo bows gratefully with her hands together.

bubbles.translation: It's fine. We're neighbors, after all!

tokens.note: -잖아요 = 'you know… / after all', reminding someone of something obvious.
Target word: 감사합니다 = 'thank you'. The ending is formal, but everyone uses it every day.

panels.image_prompt: Inside Jisoo's small, still-empty one-room studio: Minho sets down a heavy box with exaggerated effort and a sweat drop on his face; Jisoo, embarrassed, scratches her cheek next to a stack of boxes with books peeking out.

bubbles.translation: Wow, this box is really heavy!
Sorry... I have a lot of books.

panels.image_prompt: Evening at Jisoo's open apartment door: Minho stands in the hallway waving goodbye with a warm smile; Jisoo, tired but happy, bows slightly. Orange sunset light from the hallway window.

bubbles.translation: You must be tired, right? Get some good rest tonight.

tokens.note: Target word: 피곤하다 = to be tired. -죠 asks for agreement: '…, right?'
푹 쉬다 = to rest well; 푹 자다 = to sleep soundly.
Target word: 쉬다 = to rest. -세요 makes a soft, polite request.

bubbles.translation: Thanks, Minho. I hope we'll be good neighbors!

tokens.note: 고마워요 is a warm everyday 'thanks', softer than 감사합니다.
Name + 씨 is a polite way to address people your age; never use it with your own name.

tokens.translation: I hope we get along (please treat me well)
tokens.lemma_translation: please take good care of me (set phrase)
tokens.note: Set phrase for the start of a new relationship: with a neighbor, coworker or classmate.

panels.image_prompt: Night: Jisoo sits on the floor of her small studio among half-opened boxes, holding a warm mug, looking out of the window at the glowing Seoul city lights and N Seoul Tower in the distance, smiling softly.

bubbles.text: 새 집, 새 이웃. 서울 생활 시작!
bubbles.translation: A new home, a new neighbor. Life in Seoul begins!
